about: C2a-01, pass 1: the stage C2 fields of each fourth-order theme (section 2) and the notes structure.md needs. `changed` is the one sentence saying what this material's version cannot do that the source's can (for a coined theme, that nothing was borrowed); `mistaken_for` what a reader may take it for; `question` what it answers that no member answers alone; `outside` what falls outside it, with one near case; `least_sure` the member I was least sure of, with both sides.

T4-001.changed: Goffman's keying can be agreed by everyone in a strip of activity; here a whole sub is keyed for a day, and members cannot tell case by case whether a claim is inside the frame.
T4-001.mistaken_for: A fabrication (Goffman's deception) or Bateson's play between two players: this frame is announced and public, and it lies over a venue, not a pair.
T4-001.question: On whose terms a room's talk is read for a day: whether any claim in the sub, a call to the canvas included, is meant.
T4-001.outside: The sub's ordinary jokes on any other day (T3-031, playing the room's in-jokes, in Frame bridging); near case: a member's running meme played around the canvas work, which is not a frame laid over the sub.
T4-001.least_sure: T3-106, calling a network boycott: an earnest answer to a company's play (inside, as a reply to the frame) or a protest that has left the frame (outside, a sanction).

T4-002.changed: Gieryn's boundary-work wins or loses authority before an audience; here the community draws the line for itself, and no audience awards it.
T4-002.mistaken_for: Moderation or gatekeeping as such: removals belong here only when they draw the line between the sub's business and the event.
T4-002.question: Where the event may be talked about in a standing community and whether the canvas work is the community's or a side project of some of its members.
T4-002.outside: Moving the room's planning into a chat (Backstage decision-making); near case: a Discord set up for the canvas work, which moves deliberation rather than containing the event.
T4-002.least_sure: T3-090, opening a canvas sub: containment (it moves the canvas talk out) or a new venue for the work (it gives the work its own place).

T4-003.changed: Weick's sensemaking acts on an equivocal world the actors keep living in; here the object is gone in 72 hours, so an account is rarely tested by its consequences.
T4-003.mistaken_for: Sensegiving (Gioia and Chittipeddi): explaining the canvas to a newcomer looks like it, but the explainer holds no position to give sense from.
T4-003.question: How a room builds a working account of a novel, changing object well enough to place a first pixel and to read its own corner.
T4-003.outside: Recounting what happened to the work (Collective memory); near case: a member explaining after the close what a detail of the final canvas showed.
T4-003.least_sure: T3-052, remarking on neighbouring pictures: sense made of the canvas (inside) or the start of a relation with a neighbour (outside, in Order without law).

T4-004.changed: In Snow and colleagues, frame bridging recruits outsiders to a movement; here the frame is the room's own and the bridge recruits no one beyond it.
T4-004.mistaken_for: In-group humour, or culture as such: the construct holds only the traffic between a frame the room had and the new episode.
T4-004.question: How a room makes a strangers' event its own, by telling it in the frames it already holds.
T4-004.outside: The play frame of April Fools (Keying); near case: a fake patch note on 1 April, a new frame laid over the sub for the day, not an old one carried onto the canvas.
T4-004.least_sure: T3-179, arguing ideology from the canvas: an imported frame (inside) or sense made of the event as a whole (Sensemaking).

T4-005.changed: Resource mobilization assumes organizations that hold and allocate resources; here no one can hold a member's minutes or allocate them.
T4-005.mistaken_for: Recruitment, or Olson's selective incentives: the call here offers no incentive beyond the work itself.
T4-005.question: How a room turns a crowd's attention into placed pixels when no one can be ordered to place.
T4-005.outside: Asking other rooms, as rooms, for help (Reciprocity); near case: a room asking a neighbour to defend its flag, which is a request between rooms, not a call to members.
T4-005.least_sure: T3-167, timing a mass placement together: a call (inside) or a coordination device (Coordination without command).

T4-006.changed: Durkheim's emblem is sacred and stable across generations; here it is chosen in hours, can be erased by strangers, and is replaced if lost.
T4-006.mistaken_for: Branding or logo design: the choice is argued as what the room is, not as what will sell.
T4-006.question: What the room will show of itself, and so what it will act on.
T4-006.outside: Building the homeland's flag (Flagging the nation); near case: a national room whose emblem is fixed before the canvas opens, where no choice is argued.
T4-006.least_sure: T3-169, signing the sub's name: making the emblem legible as the room's (inside) or marking a territory (Territoriality).

T4-007.changed: In insect stigmergy the trace triggers a fixed response; here the trace is read and argued about, and a half-built picture can call some and repel others.
T4-007.mistaken_for: Imitation or herding: placers here respond to what the work lacks, not to what others are doing.
T4-007.question: How a mark coordinates its own completion once it is begun.
T4-007.outside: A template that fixes the output in advance (Standardization of output); near case: an anchor coordinate posted before anything stands.
T4-007.least_sure: T3-041, extending the room's work: growth read off the canvas (inside) or a new proposal (Collective representation).

T4-008.changed: Mintzberg's standardization assumes a technostructure that sets and enforces the standard; here anyone may post a template and no one can enforce it.
T4-008.mistaken_for: Planning or direct supervision: the template binds by reference, not by an order.
T4-008.question: How strangers who never speak place toward one picture.
T4-008.outside: The scripts that place a template automatically (Workarounds); near case: a bot reading the template, which multiplies hands rather than informing them.
T4-008.least_sure: T3-008, messaging individual placers to stop: enforcing the standard (inside) or restraining a neighbour's placer (Live and let live).

T4-009.changed: Gasser's workarounds bend a system the users must keep using for their own work; here the workaround is aimed at the event's central fairness rule and is contested as cheating.
T4-009.mistaken_for: Cheating or rule-breaking as such: the construct also holds the room's governance of its scripts.
T4-009.question: How a room places faster than its members can under a fixed rate limit, and how it governs the machines it builds.
T4-009.outside: A planted script that attacks a rival (Repertoire of contention); near case: a disguised script, which uses the same machine to harm another room.
T4-009.least_sure: T3-074, working around the timer: a workaround of the clock (inside) or a member's strain under it (Collective efficacy).

T4-010.changed: Goffman's back region is hidden from the audience by design; here the backstage is often public to anyone who follows a link, and rivals spy on it.
T4-010.mistaken_for: Oligarchy (Michels): the backstage concentrates decision but appoints no one.
T4-010.question: Where the room decides when it moves deliberation out of the public thread, and whether those decisions bind the rest.
T4-010.outside: Meeting other rooms in chat (Meta-organization); near case: a shared council of several rooms, where the chat holds rooms, not members.
T4-010.least_sure: T3-114, disputing the chat's authority: a dispute about the backstage (inside) or about who may decide at all (Decided order).

T4-011.changed: Ahrne and Brunsson's decided elements bind members who accept the organization; here a decided leader or vote binds no placer who does not choose to follow.
T4-011.mistaken_for: Formal organization or bureaucracy: one decided element does not make a formal organization.
T4-011.question: Where, and how rarely, a room decides an element of its own order.
T4-011.outside: Canvas-born factions' loyalty and schism (Neo-tribes); near case: hails to a colour, which bind by affect, not by decision.
T4-011.least_sure: T3-125, saying the room wings it: the stated absence of decided order (inside, as its null pole) or a remark on the room's strength (Collective efficacy).

T4-012.changed: Bandura's collective efficacy is a belief that predicts performance in stable groups; here it is voiced in passing by members who may leave the next minute.
T4-012.mistaken_for: Morale: the construct holds judgements about capability, not mood.
T4-012.question: Whether the room believes it has the hands and room for its work, and how that belief shapes whether hands come.
T4-012.outside: Weighing a fight for a lost spot against moving (Territoriality); near case: a room deciding to move after a loss, which acts on the judgement rather than voicing it.
T4-012.least_sure: T3-181, quitting the effort under strain: a voiced judgement (inside) or an exit that ends a member's part (outside, an act).

T4-013.changed: Jackson's repair is done by those who own or tend a system; here anyone can repair or damage the same pixels, and repair is never finished before the clock stops.
T4-013.mistaken_for: Defence or vigilance alone: the construct also holds routine upkeep with no attacker.
T4-013.question: What keeps a finished work alive on a surface anyone can change.
T4-013.outside: Relocating after the spot is lost (Territoriality); near case: a room moving its logo after it is overrun, where keeping the old work has been given up.
T4-013.least_sure: T3-141, covering the night shift: repair by time (inside) or a temporal coordination of its own (the form pass's finding on timing).

T4-014.changed: Brown and colleagues' territoriality protects objects an organization assigns or recognizes; here no authority recognizes any claim, so a claim holds only as long as others honour it.
T4-014.mistaken_for: Property rights or possession: nothing here is owned, only claimed.
T4-014.question: How a room claims, grants, yields and abandons a place on a finite surface that no one owns.
T4-014.outside: Growing into a neighbour's space (Repertoire of contention); near case: expansion over another flag, a claim made by attack.
T4-014.least_sure: T3-012, granting a neighbour room: a territorial grant (inside) or a host's admission (Meta-organization).

T4-015.changed: Ashworth's trench system rested on months of repeated encounters; here neighbours meet for hours, so restraint must form fast and is broken by members who never agreed to it.
T4-015.mistaken_for: Pacifism or an explicit truce: the restraint here needs no agreement.
T4-015.question: Why the open canvas was not a war of all against all.
T4-015.outside: Agreed truces (Negotiated order); near case: a written non-aggression pact, restraint by agreement rather than by tacit reciprocity.
T4-015.least_sure: T3-076, reining in the room's attackers: a move in the tacit cycle (inside) or a room enforcing an agreement on its own members (Negotiated order) or a sanction (Decided order).

T4-016.changed: Strauss's negotiated order lives inside an organization whose rules frame the bargaining; here no rule frames it and no party can deliver its members.
T4-016.mistaken_for: Diplomacy or treaty-making as such: the construct also holds disputes over who may speak for a room.
T4-016.question: How explicit, renegotiable order is made between rooms that cannot bind their own placers.
T4-016.outside: Disowning placers outside the plan (Attribution); near case: a room telling a neighbour that the vandals are not theirs, which reads a change rather than negotiating.
T4-016.least_sure: T3-126, disputing who speaks for rooms: a problem of negotiation (inside) or of decided order (Decided order).

T4-017.changed: Gouldner's norm rests on a moral community that sanctions defaulters; here a defaulter can vanish, and only the room's memory sanctions.
T4-017.mistaken_for: Altruism, or barter alone: the construct holds both sides of an obligation, freely given and traded.
T4-017.question: How rooms that compel no one count on hands beyond their own members.
T4-017.outside: Named alliances (Meta-organization); near case: an alliance for joint defence, where help is pooled by membership rather than returned.
T4-017.least_sure: T3-122, sending greetings to another room: a gift that opens an obligation (inside) or courtesy with no account (outside).

T4-018.changed: Ahrne and Brunsson's meta-organizations have formal members and decided rules; here membership in a host or alliance is often one permission, revocable by anyone's pixels.
T4-018.mistaken_for: Alliance or coalition: the construct holds bodies of rooms that decide something for their members, hosts included.
T4-018.question: How rooms organize as bodies of rooms, and how a room's standing comes to depend on another room's approval.
T4-018.outside: Canvas-born colour factions (Neo-tribes); near case: the void, a body of individual placers rather than of rooms.
T4-018.least_sure: T3-153, meeting other rooms in chat: a shared council (inside) or a backstage (Backstage decision-making).

T4-019.changed: Attribution theory studies individuals inferring causes; here the inference is made in public by a crowd with no access to who placed a pixel.
T4-019.mistaken_for: Blame: the construct also holds exoneration and the disowning of one's own placers.
T4-019.question: How a room decides what a change to its work was, and so how it answers it.
T4-019.outside: Grievances kept after the close (Rivalry); near case: blaming a rival room for a lost work days later, which keeps a relationship rather than reading a change.
T4-019.least_sure: T3-188, disowning placers outside the plan: an attribution (inside) or a limit on what a room's word covers in a deal (Negotiated order).

T4-020.changed: Tilly's repertoires change over decades; here a repertoire is learned in hours by copying.
T4-020.mistaken_for: Aggression or vandalism as such: the construct holds the recurring forms, not the motives.
T4-020.question: What moves a room had to hand when it chose to contest others' work.
T4-020.outside: Converting a neighbour's art as adoption (Collective representation, T3-175); near case: a room claiming a stray symbol as its mascot, taking a sign without attacking it.
T4-020.least_sure: T3-061, pushing into a neighbour's space: an attack (inside) or a territorial claim (Territoriality).

T4-021.changed: Kilduff and colleagues' rivalry builds over years of repeated competition; here a rivalry can form in a day, and many carry in from outside.
T4-021.mistaken_for: Competition: rivalry is a relationship with one particular other room.
T4-021.question: Why some fights went far beyond what the space was worth.
T4-021.outside: A community's own quarrel carried onto the canvas (Frame bridging, T3-086); near case: two factions of one fandom fighting in pixels, a prior quarrel bridged in rather than a canvas rivalry.
T4-021.least_sure: T3-058, blaming attackers after the close: a rivalry kept (inside) or an attribution made (Attribution).

T4-022.changed: Billig's flagging works because it goes unnoticed; here the flag is made on purpose and noticed by everyone.
T4-022.mistaken_for: Nationalism as ideology: the construct holds the practice of making and keeping the flag, not doctrines.
T4-022.question: What membership national rooms brought to the canvas, and why they organized fast and fought hard.
T4-022.outside: Arguing over a political or religious symbol (Symbolic boundaries); near case: covering a swastika near a national flag, which draws a moral line rather than flagging a nation.
T4-022.least_sure: T3-142, making ethnic jokes about rivals: national othering (inside) or a moral transgression the rooms judge (Symbolic boundaries).

T4-023.changed: Maffesoli's tribes form around lifestyles over time; here a tribe forms around a colour in hours and ends with the canvas.
T4-023.mistaken_for: Fandom or a social movement: the tribe exists only on and for the canvas.
T4-023.question: What collectives the canvas grew for itself, and how other rooms met them.
T4-023.outside: A host that admits rooms (Meta-organization); near case: the green lattice ruling on a room's request, a body of rooms rather than a tribe of placers.
T4-023.least_sure: T3-137, joining an outside group's build: belonging to a tribe (inside) or giving help to another room (Reciprocity).

T4-024.changed: Lamont and Molnár's symbolic boundaries can become social ones with institutional backing; here no institution backs them, and they hold only while someone covers the symbol.
T4-024.mistaken_for: Moderation or censorship: the line is drawn with pixels on a shared surface, by any room.
T4-024.question: How a surface with no written rules on content kept, mostly, to rules no one had written.
T4-024.outside: Taunts between rivals (Rivalry); near case: mockery of a rival room that no one judges, which keeps a relationship rather than drawing a line.
T4-024.least_sure: T3-177, calling to draw swastikas: the transgression the line answers (inside, as its opposite pole) or an attack (Repertoire of contention).

T4-025.changed: Coined, this corpus's: nothing was borrowed to change. It names returns a room courts and fears but cannot control.
T4-025.mistaken_for: Publicity, or signalling (Spence 1973). A signal is sent to inform a receiver's choice; these are returns a room courts, counts and fears from an audience it does not choose.
T4-025.question: What being seen by the whole site brings back to a community.
T4-025.outside: Adopting the mark as the sub's emblem (Transition); near case: the banner redrawn from the canvas work, which carries the work inward rather than returning an audience.
T4-025.least_sure: T3-051, pushing posts up the rankings: courting an audience (inside) or calling hands by visibility (Mobilization).

T4-026.changed: Collins's rituals need bodies co-present; here strangers share only a thread and an image, so the ritual's solidarity may not outlast the thread.
T4-026.mistaken_for: Celebration as such: the construct also holds credit, own parts, rewards and reflection.
T4-026.question: How a room pays members no one could pay, and makes strangers' pixels into 'we did it'.
T4-026.outside: Mourning the lost work (Collective memory); near case: grief for an erased logo, which keeps a record rather than marking a success.
T4-026.least_sure: T3-159, rewarding helpers with prizes: part of the marking (inside) or an incentive to mobilize (Mobilization).

T4-027.changed: Halbwachs's memory is carried by groups that persist; here the group carrying the memory may dissolve the next day.
T4-027.mistaken_for: Archiving: the record is shaped by what the room needs to remember.
T4-027.question: How a three-day effort outlived the surface it was made on.
T4-027.outside: Carrying the work to a later canvas (Transition); near case: a plan to rebuild next year, which carries the work forward rather than recording it.
T4-027.least_sure: T3-073, reporting how the work fared: a record (inside) or live repair talk (Repair work) when made before the close.

T4-028.changed: Lundin and Soderholm's transition is planned from the start of a temporary organization; here no one planned an end, so what passes on is found, not designed.
T4-028.mistaken_for: Legacy or succession: the construct holds what moves into lasting bodies at the end.
T4-028.question: Which forms outlived the clock.
T4-028.outside: Handing the work over during the event (Decided order, T3-187); near case: a leader passing maintainership before the close, a succession rather than a passage at the end.
T4-028.least_sure: T3-131, arguing over selling canvas art: passage of the product into private hands (inside) or a dispute over credit (Completion ritual).
